blurb: `by A | B` tries the actors in order and the first that verifies the caller wins. Which one that was is only known when a request arrives, so the handler learns it through the binder and `match`es on it. With no binder the answer would be thrown away and the sum would do nothing a single actor does not. Add one, `by who: A | B`, and match `who` in the body. A single actor needs no binder.
example:
on GET("/x") () -> Effect[HttpResult[String]] by User | Visitor {       // ✗ which one was it?

on GET("/x") () -> Effect[HttpResult[String]] by who: User | Visitor {   // ✓ `who` is the resolved actor
summary: A multi-actor sum `by` clause has no binder to match the resolved actor.
